The user wants to find a Golomb ruler with 9 marks.
A Golomb ruler is a set of integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ such that $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_n$ and all differences $a_j - a_i$ (for $1 \le i < j \le n$) are distinct.
The first mark must be at position 0, so $a_1 = 0$.
The number of marks is $n=9$.
The number of pairwise distances is $\binom{9}{2} = \frac{9 \times 8}{2} = 36$.
So we need 9 integers $0 = a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_9$ such that the set $\{a_j - a_i \mid 1 \le i < j \le 9\}$ has size 36.
